newsitem.title: USA: CNA executives resign over harassment allegations.
newsitem.headline: CNA executives resign over harassment allegations.

text.p: CNA Financial Corp. said that two executives of its CNA Life division have resigned following an inquiry conducted by the company of harassment allegations by two women employees.
CNA said that Jack Kettler, CNA Life president, and Robert Teske, chief administrative officer, resigned, effective March 1.

The resignations were linked by CNA to an inquiry into allegations by two women at CNA Life's operations in Nashville, Tenn. The allegations concerned offensive comments allegedly made by Kettler and Teske's alleged attempts to prevent the employees' efforts to remedy the situation, CNA said.
Roger Morris, a CNA spokesman, declined Wednesday to give further details, other than to say the investigation involved allegedly "offensive comments."

The two women, who were not identified, have not asked for any financial payments, nor has any offer been made by CNA, Morris said. He added that he was not aware of any legal action or filing made with Equal Employment Opportunity Commission.
"We worked hard to do the right thing," Morris said, adding that the women employees have returned to work.
"During the inquiry the company provided them (the women) with time off with pay and they chose to take some of that," Morris said.
He did not disclose the women's positions at CNA Life nor if they reported directly to Kettler or Teske.

It was not known when the offensive comments were allegedly made by Kettler. However, complaints were filed to Teske within the past month, Morris said. Those complaints, however, were not acted upon, he added.

When the allegations came to the attention "of the rest of the company," an inquiry was made immediately, which resulted in the executives' resignation, Morris said. He would not say if they resigned voluntarily or if they were asked to resign.

Management appointments to replace Kettler and Teske are expected to be announced soon, Morris said. CNA Life is a unit of CNA Insurance, which is part of CNA Financial, the Chicago-based holding company.
With 1996 revenues of $17 billion, CNA ranks among the top U.S. insurance groups.
